summary: Frontend hydration issue reproduced and isolated. Root cause was Next.js dev-origin blocking for local origin; external now hydrates and interactions work. Applied minimal frontend config fix in next.config.mjs.

integration_issues.issue: GET /api/v1/health returns 502 in browser console because backend is unavailable in this environment

action_items: Keep allowedDevOrigins merged with localhost/127.0.0.1 and preview hosts to avoid hydration regressions in dev/proxy setups.
If desired, suppress landing-console noise by handling /api/v1/health failures silently (currently expected with backend offline).
critical_code_review_comments: Hydration failure was environment/config-driven (allowedDevOrigins), not landing component logic.
LandingControls state logic is functional once client runtime initializes; no selector/functionality bug found in component.
context_for_next_testing_agent: External URL hydration is stable (5/5 theme-toggle passes). Local 127.0.0.1 hydration also works after config patch. Remaining console 502s are from /api/v1/health because backend is intentionally unavailable/MOCKED fallback mode.
rca of the issue: Repro before fix: local run showed WebSocket/HMR handshake errors and theme menu did not open (aria-expanded stayed false). Supervisor err log also showed 'Blocked cross-origin request to Next.js dev resource /_next/hmr from 127.0.0.1'. External initially had similar origin-block symptoms historically. Root cause: allowedDevOrigins list depended on env and did not robustly include all dev/proxy origins. Mitigation applied: next.config.mjs now merges default origins (127.0.0.1, localhost, preview domains) with env-defined origins. Verification: local and external both show [HMR] connected and landing theme menu opens (aria-expanded=true).
